title: FootprintReport
description:
One project's checkouts, what each holds, and what can go (ADR "Agent
footprint", §4).

bare.description: `main` is a bare repository: it has no checkout of its own and is not walked.

checkouts.description: The main checkout first (unless bare), then each worktree, largest first.

clean_roots.description:
The folders `ddc clean` would review to remove what is selected: the
main checkout only, never a parent of a worktree outside it.

harness.description: The coding agents' data of the last home scan; absent with `harness_reason`.

listing_error.description:
Why `git worktree list` gave no answer; absent when it did. Without
it only the main checkout and what lies inside it are reported.

main.description: The main checkout, or the bare repository.

not_scanned.description: Worktrees git lists that the walk did not read.

outside_main.description:
Selected findings outside the main checkout, which `ddc clean <main>`
does not reach: the app's Review window lists them.

oneOf.description: Selected now under the six conditions.

It fails only condition 2 (a live lock, or in use) or 3 (used within
the window), and its probes found it otherwise removable: an estimate
that assumes it stays as it is.
Anything else, with its reason.

BuildBy.description: Why a build is in use.

oneOf.description: A launcher points to it.
A process of the user runs it.
Claude Code's installer lock names a live process for it.
The newest build.

BuildsCause.description: Why no build of a harness can be told free: each locks them all.

oneOf.description: No launcher: the build in use cannot be told.

The launcher does not resolve inside the folder (a custom one, or
builds moved by `XDG_DATA_HOME`).
A process of the user named as the harness could not be inspected.
A readable process of another user carries the harness's name.
`/proc` hides other users' processes (Linux `hidepid`).
The home is on a network filesystem, which other machines may run builds from.
Photos, backups, downloads, messengers.

CheckoutEntry.description: One checkout: its state and the findings inside it.

bucket.description: Where it counts; absent for the main checkout, which counts in no bucket.

bytes.description:
The checkout's own bytes and every finding inside it; for the main
checkout, its findings only (not the size of its files).

findings.description:
The findings inside it, not in a nested checkout; the checkout's own
`git.worktree` finding is not among them.

hint.description: Why, in words, as `ddc scan` says it.

lock.description: Its `git worktree lock`, when it has one.

origin.description:
Who made it; absent for the main checkout and for a worktree kept by
an exclude or a `.ddc-keep` marker (a claim, not a worktree region).

reason.description: Why it is held back; with `bucket: held-back` only.

worktree.description: The six conditions' facts, as `ddc scan` reports them.

oneOf.description: A linked worktree.
A `.git` file into a gitdir that is gone (`git.worktree-orphan`).

Contents.description:
The direct children of a folder with entries: the largest listed, the
rest summed. A session folder's entry is a session: its transcript (or
its folder in `file-history`) with the siblings named after it.

entries.description:
Largest first (ties by path bytes); at most 100. A user-data folder's
are each at least 10 MiB; a session folder's have no floor.

rest_count.description: The other children, findings of their own left out.

EntryLock.description: Why an entry cannot be picked. One type in the scan report and the clean report.

oneOf.description: An app manages it; clean it in that app.
A `.ddc-keep` in it, or an exclude at or in it.
A protected folder (safety ADR §6) at or inside it.
Another volume is mounted inside it.

It, or something inside it, has an immutable or append-only flag: its
owner cannot remove it (safety ADR, amendment of 2026-11-04, "Linux
file kinds").
Added or changed within [`RECENT`] of the scan's start: in use or still arriving.
A download still arriving.
A backup whose `Status.plist` does not say it finished.

A coding agent's session that is live: a live record names it, a
file of it changed within [`RECENT`], or a process holds one open.
In place of `recent` for the session folders.

Whether the session is live could not be told: the harness's live
records could not be read or decided.

A coding agent's build still needed: a launcher points to it, a
process of the user runs it, its installer lock names a live process,
or it is the newest.

Whether any build of the harness is still needed could not be told:
every build is locked.

Exclusion.description: An exclusion or a skip that protects a finding, canonical.

inside.description:
The path lies inside the finding; otherwise it is the finding's own
folder or above it.

oneOf.description: Never touched (`excludes`, `--exclude`).
Never read (`skips`, `--skip`).
`settings.json`.
A command-line flag.

bytes.description:
Allocated bytes belonging to this finding alone. On Linux btrfs with
compression it is the uncompressed size, which can be far more than a
delete frees; on ZFS it is the size on disk after compression. A
delete frees nothing of the blocks a snapshot still holds.

class.description: Effective class (may be lower than `rule_class`, see `notes`).

contents.description:
What one of the user's own folders holds, to pick from (story "User
data: pick your own files for the Trash"), or the sessions of a
coding agent's session folder (story "Harness data rules"). Only on
findings of a rule with an entry policy (`rules::entries::policy`)
the scan could read.

dev.description:
The device, with `ino` the identity at scan time: `st_dev`, except
on Linux btrfs and ZFS, where it is the filesystem's `f_fsid` folded
into 64 bits, which a remount keeps and the anonymous `st_dev` does
not.

ignored.description:
Hidden by `settings.json`: its rule is switched off, or it is under
`min_size`. Never selected and in no total; `not_selected` is unchanged.

incomplete.description: Some content could not be read or was skipped; sizes are lower bounds.

modified.description:
The newest modification time inside it, its own directory included,
RFC 3339 in UTC to the second (story "Review window: sort a group's
rows by name, size or last change"). A lower bound when `incomplete`.
Only inside a claim the walk read times for: none on a region, a
user-data finding, a protected one, an unlisted rule's, or one whose
root could not be opened.

not_selected.description:
Why it is not selected by default. An ignored finding keeps the reason
it would have had, so a type switched back on applies at once.

origin.description:
The harness whose own structure the rule recognizes (ADR "Agent
footprint: worktrees, harness data and bounded consent for agents",
§1). Only on findings of such rules, and on every git worktree's,
whose harness the worktree itself tells (§2).

parent_dev.description: Identity of the parent directory at scan time (re-checked before cleaning).

private_bytes.description:
Lower bound of what deleting it frees (APFS private size). Present
where clones are expected (uv, pnpm) and measurable.

protection.description:
What keeps a `user.kept` finding (story "Protected by you: say what it
is, and Remove Protection"). Only on those findings.

selected.description: Selected by default in a cleanup plan.

shared_bytes.description: Allocated bytes of hard-linked files also linked elsewhere.

worktree.description:
What the scan read of a linked git worktree (ADR "Agent footprint:
worktrees, harness data and bounded consent for agents", §2). Only on
`git.worktree` findings.

FolderEntry.description:
One direct child of a folder with entries: a regular file or a
directory. A session's entry is its key (`<session>.jsonl`, or
`<session>/` in `file-history`), with its companions' bytes.

backup.description: A device backup's `Info.plist`, where it could be read.

bytes.description:
Allocated bytes, findings inside it included; a session's, its
companions' too. Counted as a finding's `bytes` is, with the same
compression and snapshot caveats.

dev.description:
The device, with `ino` the identity at scan time: `st_dev`, except
on Linux btrfs and ZFS, where it is the filesystem's `f_fsid` folded
into 64 bits, which a remount keeps and the anonymous `st_dev` does
not.

findings.description: Findings of other rules inside it (a folder in Downloads).

incomplete.description:
Parts of it could not be read; `bytes` is a lower bound. It can still
be picked: the Trash keeps it.

modified.description:
Last modification, RFC 3339; a session's, the newest of its files'
own.

FootprintTotals.description: Bytes by class, and what can go.

held_back.description:
The worktrees of `bucket: held-back`, without what inside them is
selected now. No byte is in two of these sums.

reclaimable_after_sessions.description:
The worktrees of `bucket: after-sessions`, without what inside them
is selected now (counted in `reclaimable_now`): an estimate.

reclaimable_now.description:
Selected now: `safe` items (an agent may clean them once the person's
opt-in is on) apart from `rebuildable` ones (the person's), a selected
worktree with everything inside it.

safe.description: Every finding inside the checkouts, by class; each byte once.

HarnessPart.description: What the last home scan found of the coding agents' own data.

report_age.description: Seconds since that scan was written.

oneOf.description: No `last-scan.json` in the data directory.
It was written by another report schema.
It could not be read or decoded.

HeldReason.description:
Why a checkout is held back: the first condition that fails, or why it
is not judged at all.

oneOf.description: Locked, and its lock names no pid or one that does not run.
Copied or moved by hand: git does not know it there.
Made by a harness whose worktrees ddc does not select.
Its gitdir is gone.
The person's own worktree.
A file inside it is immutable.
Not the current user's.
Under an exclude, or holding `.ddc-keep`.
Under `min_size` in `settings.json`.
Nothing tells when it was last used.
`git.worktree` is switched off in `settings.json`.

IgnoredContent.description:
The ignored paths that hold a worktree back: the first ones, and how
many there are in all.

LiveBy.description:
What shows a session live. The scan report's `live-session` lock
carries it as `by`.

oneOf.description: A live record names it.

Its transcript or a companion changed within [`entries::RECENT`]
before the check, or later than it.
A process of the user holds one of its files open.

Lock.description: A `git worktree lock` and whether its holder runs.

live.description:
Whether that pid runs as the current user: an estimate, since the
pid may have been reused. Absent without a pid, or without a process
table on this platform; then a lock with a pid is taken as live.

pid.description: The pid its reason names (`(pid N`); absent when it names none.

MarkerFolder.description: A folder holding a `.ddc-keep`, with its identity at scan time.

dev.description:
The device, with `ino` the identity at scan time: `st_dev`, except
on Linux btrfs and ZFS, where it is the filesystem's `f_fsid` folded
into 64 bits, which a remount keeps and the anonymous `st_dev` does
not.

NotScanned.description: A worktree git lists that the walk did not read.

oneOf.description: Under a skip of `settings.json` or the command line.
git lists it and the folder is gone, or does not resolve.
On another filesystem than its parent.
Read, but not recognised as a worktree.
Expensive to restore or restorability uncertain: always a manual choice.
The user's data: never planned.
The project changed recently.
No activity signal: treated as active.

Something inside, or the folder itself, belongs to another user (a
container's root, say): never selected, never removed (safety ADR,
amendment of 2026-10-31).

Something inside, or the folder itself, has an immutable or
append-only flag: its owner cannot remove it, and a folder holding
one can never be emptied. Never selected, never removed (safety ADR,
amendment of 2026-11-04, "Linux file kinds").
Environment without a lock file: restoring may give a different environment.
Inside a hidden top-level folder of $HOME or ~/Library: owned by an app or tool.
A `.ddc-keep` marker in it or above it.
Matched `--exclude`.

Origin.description:
Where a finding comes from: a coding agent's harness and what of it the
finding is. A provenance, not a class: the class and the method decide
what happens to it.

oneOf.description: A git worktree, whoever made it.
A worktree an agent works in.
What the harness keeps of its sessions: transcripts, history, logs.
What the harness downloads or writes for itself and can make again.

What the harness installs for itself and fetches again only by hand:
its old builds (safety ADR, amendment of 2026-11-02).

Project.description:
The project an artifact belongs to, and how recently it changed. On a
`git.worktree` finding `root` is the worktree's main checkout, while
`last_activity` and `idle_days` are the worktree's own (its gitdir's
index and `HEAD`, its manifests and lock files), never the main
checkout's.

last_activity.description: Latest activity (RFC 3339): git index/HEAD, manifests, lock files.

worktree_of.description:
The main checkout, when `root` is a linked git worktree of it: the
report groups the worktree's artifacts under the main project.

Protection.description:
What protects a `user.kept` finding: its keep markers, the exclusions and
skips at or above it or inside it, and the rule it displaced.

markers.description:
Each folder holding a `.ddc-keep`, the finding's own or one inside it,
sorted by folder.

rule.description:
The rule that would have claimed the folder, when the walk knows it.
Under an exclusion at or above the folder nothing is listed, so only a
known path, a region or a child of a known path is known there.

oneOf.description: Cache that refills itself.
Project artifact restored by install (from a lock file) or by a build.
Expensive to restore, or restorability is uncertain.
The user's data: reported, never planned.

UnknownCause.description:
Why a session's liveness could not be told. Declared from the widest
to the narrowest: when several apply, the first is reported. The scan
report's `liveness-unknown` lock carries it as `cause`.

oneOf.description:
The records folder does not exist: an older Claude Code, or a
changed layout.
The records folder, or an entry of it, could not be read.

The records folder lies at or under one of the user's skips, so it
is never opened.
A record could not be parsed.
A record could not be decided and names no session.
A live record names no session.
A record that could not be decided names this session.
The session was given with no file, so nothing could be checked.

WorktreeProbe.description:
Whether a worktree's git probes ran and were understood. `unknown` fails
closed: the worktree stays `review`.

WorktreeState.description:
A linked git worktree's state. The fields a git probe fills are absent
until one ran; `probe` says whether it did.

branch.description:
The branch checked out, without `refs/heads/`; absent when `HEAD` is
detached or could not be read.

clean.description: No tracked change and no untracked file.

detached.description: `HEAD` names a commit, not a branch; absent when it could not be read.

idle_days.description: Days since its own last activity.

ignored_content.description:
Ignored paths nothing accounts for: neither inside an artifact ddc
removes on its own nor a copy of the main checkout's file.

in_use.description: A process of the current user works inside it.

linked.description:
Its administrative folder's back-pointer (`<gitdir>/gitdir`) names
this folder's `.git`, by file identity. False for a worktree copied
or moved by hand: `git worktree repair` relinks it, and ddc never
removes it through git.

locked.description: `<gitdir>/locked` exists: `git worktree lock`, or a live session's lock.

own_commits.description:
Commits reachable from its `HEAD` and from no reference that
survives its removal.

probe.description: Whether the git probes ran and were understood.

submodules.description: A submodule is initialized in it.
